blocks.text: You are not mad. You want that understood. A madman could never have planned it this carefully.
The old man never wronged you. You even liked him. It was his eye. One pale, clouded eye, like a vulture's. Every time it fell on you, your blood ran cold.
So for seven nights, at midnight, you open his door. So slowly it takes an hour. And you watch him sleep.
On the eighth night, he wakes. He sits up in the dark. And you hear it. A low, dull, quick sound. His heart. Louder. And louder.
When it is over, the heart is silent. You hide him beneath the floorboards. So neatly that no eye could find a thing.
At four in the morning, three policemen knock. A neighbour heard a cry. You smile. You show them every room. You even set their chairs right over the spot.
They sit. They chat. And then you hear it again. Low. Dull. Quick. Coming from under the floor. Louder. Louder.
They must hear it. They are only pretending not to. And you cannot bear it one second longer. You point at the boards, and scream the truth.
Based on The Tell-Tale Heart, by Edgar Allan Poe. 1843.
